svg.aria-label: Rung 1,000, designed only: a WAF and CDN edge fronts a multi-AZ API fleet, which feeds one queue per workload class; an agent fleet of about five hundred slots drains the interactive queue and calls an LLM router across providers, a separate CPU-bound sandbox fleet reads a dedicated vector store, and an online judge samples a few percent of production answers while Aurora runs a writer plus readers and cost is shown back per tenant.

g.title: queues per workload class — interactive, batch and eval-sample, so a report backfill never queues behind a live user
Aurora — one writer plus N readers; marts partitioned by tenant and dataset, with schema-per-tenant where a customer demands physical isolation
edge — CloudFront plus WAF, with per-tenant rate limits applied before anything reaches a fleet
agent fleet — about 500 slots for 1,000 askers at the same wait target, e.g. 60–120 tasks × 4–8 concurrency, autoscaled on backlog per task
LLM router — 500 concurrent calls exceeds one provider's default quota, so this is per-tenant quotas, prompt caching and fallbacks across providers
API fleet — 10–20 tasks across availability zones behind an ALB per fleet; blue/green ships on weighted target groups
sandbox fleet — CPU-bound analysis kept on its own autoscaling group, isolated from the cheap high-concurrency LLM-wait workers
vector store — pgvector graduates out of the database to a dedicated or partitioned service
online judge — samples a small percentage of production answers so a canary can be judged before it takes all the traffic
cost showback — per-tenant spend, where the budget alarm becomes a per-tenant quota

path.title: every request is admitted through a queue, never straight to a worker
